name: LTM Ltd. (erstwhile LTIMindtree)
business_summary: India's fifth/sixth-largest listed IT services company (formed by the Nov-2022 merger of L&T Infotech and Mindtree; renamed LTM), ~69% owned by Larsen & Toubro. Offers application development, cloud and infra, data/AI, ERP and digital engineering to BFSI, manufacturing, hi-tech, energy/utilities and healthcare clients, ~70% from North America. TTM sales Rs43,359 cr, EBITDA margin ~18%, debt-free, ROE ~24%. AI-linked (Enterprise/Biz AI) revenue grew ~47% YoY in Q2 FY27. Stock -22.8% over 12 months, P/E 24.6 (premium to Infosys/Wipro).

exposures.mechanism: ~93% of revenue is USD/EUR/GBP-linked while ~50-55% of costs are INR (model knowledge). +3% USD/INR adds ~1.2-1.5pp of margin pre-hedge; at 18% EBITDA margin that is +7% EBITDA; LTM has stated no hedging benefit lasts beyond ~4-6 quarters and clients/wage cycle claw ~60% back, persistence 0.35; EV/MCap ~0.95 => +2.3. Pack elasticity is NEGATIVE (-1.16, t -0.8) - not significant and driven by risk-off episodes when INR weakens and IT sells off; I keep the fundamental sign but a wide range.

evidence.note: Screener: Sep-26 qtr sales 11,276 cr, OPM 18%, 12m price -22.8%, 1y vol 34%

exposures.mechanism: North America ~70% of revenue (model knowledge). +1pp US growth => IT-services spend +1.5pp elasticity => revenue +1.0%; incremental margin 30% vs 18% => EBITDA +1.7%; growth-rate shifts are structural (persistence 1.0) and re-rate the multiple (P/E 24.6 vs peers 15-20) => +3.

evidence.note: TCS Q2 FY27 TCV $9.6bn, revenue +11% YoY INR - US discretionary spend stabilising

exposures.mechanism: SSU +1 = a step of GenAI-led repricing (~3% of revenue base). Deflation 3% at ~60% flow-through => EBITDA -10%; persistence 0.5 (volume recapture + AI revenue growth) => -5; LTM partly hedged because AI revenue grew 47% YoY in Q2 FY27 and Enterprise/Biz AI is now a disclosed line, so central -4 vs peers. Sign genuinely two-sided so range includes +3.

evidence.note: Business Today: stock -28% in 2026, pivot to short-term AI deals; AI revenue +47%

exposures.mechanism: +1 = material tightening (H-1B fee/PERM/HIRE-style outsourcing tax). Onsite visa-dependent staff ~ 15% of headcount (model knowledge), replacement via local hiring adds ~2pp to cost-of-revenue => -11% EBITDA before pass-through; 50% passed on, persistence 0.6 => ~-3.5. Observed: PERM suspension 2026-10-08 produced a rally (Reuters: <2% of filings) and the $100k H-1B fee was struck down 2026-10-01 - realised tail so far mild.

evidence.note: US suspended PERM green-card labour programme for named firms; Reuters 2026-10-11: little risk to Indian IT (<2% of green-card filings)
Forbes 2026-10-01: judge struck down latest version of $100,000 H-1B fee; Indian Express 2026-09-19: fee extended
